main_text.p: Gregorius Episcopus Nazianzenus, multo sale respersas, tandem autem concludit: [{e}eos à quibus tyrannide oppressi sumus, mansuetudine vincamus, hac ratione, eis à quibus iniurias accepimus, sublimiores nos prastamus.] Cyrillus autem Episcopus Alexandrinus in responsione ad libros Iuliani, (quos teste {f}Hieronymo in expeditione Parthica contra Christum euomuit)- in Epistola nuncupatoria ad Theodosium, non tam contra Regem se dicere profitetur, quàm pro gloria Christi, qui cum summo uniuersorum Patre suo principatum gerit, de quo & solo dici debet; per me Reges regnant.Orat.2. in IulianumEpist.84.

Postremò Milites Christiani, quod ad Idolis thurifican-dum adegit, non arma arripiunt; aut ad-uerfus eum coniurationem incunt ; fed [cùm venissent ad Principem (inquit {g}Eutropius) proiecerunt aurum, quod acceperant, & forti voce poscebant, ut reciperet quod dediffet, & occideret illos.] Tantùm abfuit illa aetas à Principe, vel omnium sceleftiffimo occidendo, ut ipfi occidi popofcerint. Necdif-similiter de hoc ipso Imperatore; & eisdem militibus {h} D. Augustinus. ]Domi-

page.notes: The first word of the page is a continuation from the previous page. The "e" and "f" reference marks are small superscript letters in the text. The Greek-free page has no catchword or signature in this part. The last line is cut off by the scan; it continues in the next part. The text mark before "Eutropius" is printed as a section-like sign; it is read here as the mark g, matching the marginal note. The catchword "mi-" is the start of the next page's word. The strikethrough dash after "Principem" is printed and read as "(inquit". The printed "Necdif-" is read as printed.
